items.q: In a right triangle with angle 30°, opposite side 5, and hypotenuse 10, find sin 30°.
hints: sin = opposite / hypotenuse.

items.q: In a right triangle with angle 45°, adjacent side 1, and hypotenuse sqrt(2), find cos 45°.
hints: cos = adjacent / hypotenuse.
1 / sqrt(2), rationalised by multiplying top and bottom by sqrt(2).
sqrt(2)/2

items.q: In a right triangle with angle 60°, opposite side sqrt(3), adjacent side 1, find tan 60°.
hints: tan = opposite / adjacent.
sqrt(3) / 1.
sqrt(3)

items.q: In a right triangle, opposite side 8 and hypotenuse 17. Find sin theta.
hints: sin = opposite / hypotenuse.

items.q: In a right triangle, adjacent side 12 and hypotenuse 13. Find cos theta.
hints: cos = adjacent / hypotenuse.

items.q: In a right triangle, opposite side 7 and adjacent side 24. Find tan theta.
hints: tan = opposite / adjacent.

items.q: In a right triangle, opposite side 3 and hypotenuse 5. Find cos theta.
hints: cos needs the adjacent side — find it first using Pythagoras.
adjacent = sqrt(5^2 - 3^2) = sqrt(16) = 4, so cos theta = 4/5.

items.q: Find the missing side: opposite = 6, angle = 30°. Use sine to find the hypotenuse.
hints: sin(angle) = opposite / hypotenuse — rearrange to find the hypotenuse.
hypotenuse = 6 / sin(30°) = 6 / 0.5.

items.q: Find the missing side: adjacent = 8, angle = 60°. Use cosine to find the hypotenuse.
hints: cos(angle) = adjacent / hypotenuse — rearrange to find the hypotenuse.
hypotenuse = 8 / cos(60°) = 8 / 0.5.

items.q: Find the missing side: opposite = 9, angle = 45°. Use tangent to find the adjacent side.
hints: tan(angle) = opposite / adjacent — rearrange to find the adjacent side.
adjacent = 9 / tan(45°) = 9 / 1.

items.q: Find the angle: opposite = 5, hypotenuse = 10.
hints: Use sin(angle) = opposite / hypotenuse, then take the inverse sine.
sin(angle) = 5/10 = 0.5.

items.q: Find the angle: adjacent = 6, hypotenuse = 12.
hints: Use cos(angle) = adjacent / hypotenuse, then take the inverse cosine.
cos(angle) = 6/12 = 0.5.

items.q: Find the angle: opposite = 1, adjacent = 1.
hints: Use tan(angle) = opposite / adjacent, then take the inverse tangent.
tan(angle) = 1/1 = 1.

items.q: A ramp rises 2 m over a horizontal distance of 10 m. Find the angle of the ramp to the nearest degree.
hints: Use tan(angle) = opposite / adjacent = rise / horizontal distance.
tan(angle) = 2/10, so angle = tan^-1(0.2).

items.q: A ladder reaches 5 m up a wall and is 12 m from the wall. Find the angle of elevation.
hints: Use tan(angle) = opposite / adjacent = height / distance.
tan(angle) = 5/12, so angle = tan^-1(5/12).

items.q: A kite is 20 m high and 20sqrt(3) m away horizontally. Find the angle of elevation.
hints: Use tan(angle) = opposite / adjacent = height / horizontal distance.
tan(angle) = 20 / (20sqrt(3)) = 1/sqrt(3).

items.q: A cliff top is seen at an angle of elevation of 45° from 30 m away. Find the height.
hints: Use tan(angle) = height / distance, then rearrange for height.
height = 30 x tan(45°) = 30 x 1.

items.q: A ship is seen at an angle of depression of 30° from a lighthouse 40sqrt(3) m high. Find the horizontal distance.
hints: The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the ship — use tan(angle) = height / distance and rearrange for distance.
distance = height / tan(30°) = 40sqrt(3) / (1/sqrt(3)).

items.q: A tree top is seen at 60° from a point 10 m away. Find the height.
hints: Use tan(angle) = height / distance, then rearrange for height.
height = 10 x tan(60°) = 10 x sqrt(3).
10sqrt(3)

items.q: A balloon is 50 m high and seen at 45°. Find the horizontal distance.
hints: Use tan(angle) = height / distance, then rearrange for distance.
distance = 50 / tan(45°) = 50 / 1.

items.q: A tower is seen at an angle of elevation of 30° from 50 m away, with the observer's eye 1.5 m above the ground. Find the tower's height to 1 d.p.
hints: Find the height above eye level using tan(angle) = height / distance, then add the eye height.
50 x tan(30°) = 28.87, so total height = 28.87 + 1.5.

items.q: A ship travels on a bearing of 090°. What direction is this?
hints: Bearings are measured clockwise from north (000°).
090° is a quarter turn clockwise from north.
East

items.q: A plane travels due south. Write the bearing.
hints: Bearings are measured clockwise from north (000°), always as 3 digits.
South is a half turn clockwise from north.

items.q: A point is north-west of another. Is the bearing 315°?
hints: Bearings are measured clockwise from north — north-west is three-quarters of the way round.
North-west is 315° clockwise from north (270° for west, plus 45° back towards north).
Yes

items.q: A town lies on a bearing of 045° from a village. What compass direction is this?
hints: Bearings are measured clockwise from north (000°).
045° is halfway between north (000°) and east (090°).
North-east

items.q: A ship travels on a bearing of 270°. What direction is this?
hints: Bearings are measured clockwise from north (000°).
270° is three-quarters of a turn clockwise from north.
West

items.q: Write the bearing for due north.
hints: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, always as 3 digits.
North itself is the starting point, 0°.

items.q: A is on a bearing of 060° from B. Find the bearing of B from A.
hints: A back bearing (the reverse direction) is found by adding or subtracting 180°.

items.q: A cuboid is 3 by 4 by 12. Find the body diagonal.
hints: Use the 3D distance formula: diagonal = sqrt(length^2 + width^2 + height^2).

items.q: A cuboid is 6 by 8 by 24. Find the body diagonal.
hints: Use the 3D distance formula: diagonal = sqrt(length^2 + width^2 + height^2).

items.q: Find the angle between the base and the diagonal of a cuboid with height 12 and base diagonal 5.
hints: Use tan(angle) = height / base diagonal, then take the inverse tangent.
tan(angle) = 12/5, so angle = tan^-1(12/5).

items.q: A ladder reaches a window 12 m above the ground and 5 m out from the wall. Find the ladder length.
hints: This is a right-angled triangle — use Pythagoras with the height and horizontal distance.

items.q: A cuboid has base diagonal 15 and height 8. Find the body diagonal.
hints: The body diagonal, base diagonal, and height form a right-angled triangle — use Pythagoras.

items.q: A cuboid is 9 by 12 by 20. Find the body diagonal.
hints: Use the 3D distance formula: diagonal = sqrt(length^2 + width^2 + height^2).
